_doc: attr-classification-overrides.json — the hand-authored, reseed-durable OVERRIDE layer for block_attributes classification corrections (role/derived_selector/css_property/css_element/css_state/css_tier/box_family/etc). Lifted verbatim from sgs-update-v2.py ATTR_CLASSIFICATION_OVERRIDES (Bean request, 2026-07-21). This is the single source of truth Bean asked for — sgs-update-v2.py now READS this file rather than declaring the dict inline. Applied AFTER the derived classifier layer (css-property-classifications.json) as Stage 1 sub-step C, so an override here wins on any field conflict with the derived layer. Records here exist to correct genuine mis-derivations OR to record cases where what the code DOES and what it MEANS differ (e.g. sgs/tabs tabIndicatorColour delivers via box-shadow but is a COLOUR value type) — never to correct plain accuracy bugs in the classifier, which should be fixed at the classifier itself. Two entries added 2026-07-21 for the value-type-vs-delivery-property fix: sgs/tabs tabIndicatorColour/tabActiveIndicatorColour resolve via the classifier chain-walk to box-shadow (render.php:84-100 colour_props array -> style.css:120 inset box-shadow underline) — accurate but unusable for a consumer picking a control type. The manifest (tabs/block.json supports.sgs.elements.tab.attrMap) already declares these as css:border-color (its own documented rationale: the active variant renders via [aria-selected='true'], not CSS :active, and drives the underline/box-shadow INDICATOR colour). css_property overridden here to border-color to match that already-established, coordinator-approved manifest vocabulary — a colour-family property a consumer control-picker can route to a colour picker, not a shadow control. 18 entries added 2026-07-22 (Spec 31 coupled UN-EXCLUDE + HOVER-LIFT): scaleHover (10 blocks, excl. sgs/post-grid whose scaleHover is a per-item css_element=card derived-selector attr with a multi-property css_property, out of this base-domain resolver channel) / grayscaleHover (4 blocks) / imageZoomHover (4 blocks incl. sgs/post-grid, whose imageZoomHover IS root-scoped) now carry css_property=transform|filter + css_state=hover — these attrs have NO un-suffixed base sibling (the effect only ever exists as a hover interaction), so the new converter.db.db_lookup.attr_for_state_property direct-lookup channel resolves them by (css_property, css_state) rather than the base+Hover-suffix-append convention tabIndicatorColour-style pairs use. 1 entry added 2026-08-02 (property_suffixes Rating/Speed suffix-role fix, migrations/2026-08-01-rating-speed-suffix-role.py): the property_suffixes 'Rating' suffix was reclassified from the wrong 'number-css-px' to the common case 'behaviour' (it is right for 3 of the 4 attrs it matches: sgs/star-rating.maxRating, sgs/google-reviews.minRating, sgs/testimonial.showRating are all configuration, not content). sgs/star-rating.rating is the one genuine exception — the star/numeric rating VALUE ITSELF, a content-bearing display value matching the existing 'rating' role's own exemplar (sgs/testimonial.ratingStars, registered by migrations/2026-06-21-register-rating-role.py). Declared here as a single-attr override rather than bending the suffix rule to fit the minority case, per this layer's job (Layer 3, applied LAST, wins over the suffix-derived role on any conflict) — see check_css_property_reseed.py's docstring for the layering contract.

entries._why: canonical_slot added 2026-09-06 (Check#12 roleguess fix). The element-scope 'icon' slot resolves to standalone_block sgs/icon, but sgs/icon carries 6 content-bearing candidates across 6 different roles (dashiconName/emojiChar/iconName/iconSource/linkTarget/wpIconName) with none owning canonical_slot='icon', so a draft child's bare __icon token fell to insertion-order guessing. iconSource (role='identity') is the block's own GENERIC icon-source field -- it already resolves via the SAME icon-slug priority chain (data-icon/data-lucide/inline-svg/BEM-modifier) as the format-specific fields, per roles.json's own 'identity' role docs -- so it is the correct sole owner of the generic 'icon' concept; the format-specific fields (dashiconName etc.) are populated separately by resolve_icon_kind()'s own dispatch, not by this slot match.

canonical_slot merged in 2026-09-06 (Check#12 roleguess fix): this attr previously carried canonical_slot='text' (a self-referential default from the attribute's own name), but the incoming slot literal for this block's registered purpose is 'disclaimer' (slots.json: 'Disclaimer/legal callout text... -> sgs/notice-banner'), which had no exact match anywhere, so it fell to guessing among {iconName, iconSource, text}. css_element PINNED 2026-08-15. The css_element reset added to sgs-update-v2.py the same day cleared this value because the derivation cannot re-derive it for THIS block: post-grid's hover-zoom rule targets `.sgs-post-grid__img` (style.css:488) while 13 other rules in the same file use `.sgs-post-grid__image`, and the manifest declares `image` — one block, two class names for one element. Without this pin `lift_per_element_state` stops routing the attr and post-grid's image hover-zoom is SILENTLY DROPPED on every clone, the exact defect converter/tests/test_per_element_state_lift.py exists to prevent (this attr is one of the five named in its docstring). DO NOT remove this pin to tidy up: fix post-grid's own `__img` vs `__image` split first, re-verify that test, THEN remove.

Track B, 2026-08-04. The `price` slot lists "ribbon" among its own aliases, and load_slot_aliases() builds its map first-writer-wins over an unordered scan, so `price` claims the name before the dedicated `ribbon` slot (which exists) can register its own. A draft authoring a cta-section ribbon writes .sgs-cta-section__ribbon, which the price-derived selector cannot match. Measured: 10 such alias collisions exist, 4 touch a live sgs/% attr, 3 are wrong. Fixed by override, NOT by de-duplicating slots.aliases: 179 of 1170 attrs depend on that alias layer for genuine synonym work (title->heading, url->link, columns->column), so removing it would break ~175 rows to fix 3.

Track B, 2026-08-04. Same alias-collision class: the `text` slot claims "caption" as an alias, so sgs/media.caption seeded canonical_slot='text'. The block genuinely renders .sgs-media__caption (verified: 2 occurrences in its own source), which is what a draft would author.

Track B, 2026-08-04. Same alias-collision class, opposite remedy: the `card` slot claims "step" as an alias, so a number field's numeric increment (e.g. 0.01) seeded canonical_slot='card'. This attr is not a content slot at all, so the correct value is NULL rather than a better slot name — matching the sgs/product-card.priceNote precedent above. Corroborated independently by the Track A fingerprint, whose D1 detector vetoed this attr after examining every usage site.

2026-09-05 Task 4 (testimonial classic-card/rating-led content-loss audit). derived_selector was NULL, so lift_scalar_content's first gate (scalar_content.py:158-160) skipped this attr before role was even consulted -- no draft, however faithfully shaped, could ever populate it. render.php:717 confirms the star-rating container carries BOTH classes together: `class="sgs-testimonial__rating sgs-testimonial__stars"` -- `.sgs-testimonial__stars` is used (not the shared `.sgs-testimonial__rating`) so this attr's selector never also matches the UNRELATED numeric-scale container (`.sgs-testimonial__rating.sgs-testimonial__rating--scale`, rating-led variant), which carries no star aria-label/glyphs at all.

2026-09-05 Task 4 (testimonial rating-led content-loss audit). derived_selector was NULL -- same missing-selector defect class as ratingStars above, blocking the attr at the data layer regardless of draft markup. role='text-content'/attr_type='string' already correctly matches lift_scalar_content's is_text gate; only the selector was missing. render.php:730 confirms the real emitted class: `<span class="sgs-testimonial__source">`.

2026-09-05 Task 4 (testimonial rating-led content-loss audit). role was 'select-from-enum', which lift_scalar_content's gate correctly excludes (an enum pick is not this attr's shape) -- but the role itself was the mis-derivation, not the gate: render.php:103-104 clamps this to a CONTINUOUS 0-100 float (`max(0, min(100, (float)$attributes['ratingScale']))`), e.g. '9.2 / 10' -- not a fixed choice set. Reusing the existing 'rating' role (its docstring says 'star/numeric') was considered and REJECTED: its sole consumer, extract_star_count() (converter/services/lift_helpers.py:112-126), hardcodes an aria-label-digit-or-glyph-count read clamped to 0..5 -- silently WRONG (not merely absent) for a 0-100 score, and this element carries no aria-label/star glyphs at all. A new role 'numeric-content' was added instead (data/roles.json, converter/services/field_extractors.py, converter/resolvers/scalar_content.py) -- zero pre-existing attrs carried it, so widening the gate to accept it changes no other block's behaviour. derived_selector narrowed from the shared '.sgs-testimonial__rating' (also matches the UNRELATED star container in classic-card, and would swallow the trailing '/ 10' text if read from the outer div) to '.sgs-testimonial__score', the exact span render.php:686 emits the numeric value into.

2026-09-05 Task 4 (testimonial rating-led content-loss audit) -- found while fixing ratingScale, not itself in the original 4-field root-cause list, but necessary for the ratingScale fix to have any visible effect: render.php:679 gates the numeric-score render branch on `'scale' === $rating_type`, and ratingType defaults to 'stars' (render.php:98) with no prior mechanism to ever set it to 'scale' from draft content. role was 'select-from-enum' (excluded by the same gate as ratingScale, for the same reason -- there is no enum PICKER here, the value is read off the draft, not chosen). The correct shape is 'css-modifier': render.php:685 emits the modifier class `sgs-testimonial__rating--scale` on the SAME element ratingScale's derived_selector's ancestor `.sgs-testimonial__rating` matches, so the value is recoverable as a BEM --modifier suffix. 'css-modifier' already existed as a role in field_extractors.py (used by array_content's per-item extraction) but had never been wired into lift_scalar_content's gate -- zero pre-existing block_attributes rows carried it, so widening the gate is a genuinely new, zero-blast-radius capability, not a change to existing behaviour. derived_selector is UNCHANGED ('.sgs-testimonial__rating', already correct) -- for classic-card's star container this element carries no `--` modifier, so extraction correctly returns None (no key emitted) and the attr's own 'stars' default applies exactly as before.

2026-09-05 Task 4 (testimonial rating-led content-loss audit). TWO independent defects stacked on this one row. (1) Wrong selector: derived_selector was '.sgs-testimonial__text', which does not exist anywhere in render.php -- the real emitted badge is `<span class="sgs-testimonial__verified">` (render.php:727). (2) Wrong role: 'boolean-visibility' -- but that role's own contract (data/roles.json) states 'a draft's HTML/CSS carries no signal a boolean toggle could be lifted from, so the absence of a resolver is expected, not a gap'. That claim is FALSE for this attr: the badge's mere presence in the draft IS a real, unambiguous signal (unlike avatarDecorative/orgLogoDecorative, genuine editor-only preference toggles with no draft signal, correctly left on 'boolean-visibility'). A new role 'presence-boolean' was added (data/roles.json, field_extractors.py, scalar_content.py) rather than repurposing 'boolean-visibility' itself, because that role is explicitly documented and relied upon elsewhere as 'no consumer, deliberately excluded from the content walk' -- widening IT would have silently started content-lifting every other attr that (correctly) carries that role. 'presence-boolean' is brand new (zero pre-existing rows), so this fix cannot change any other block's behaviour.

MIS-DERIVED css_property cleared 2026-08-29. photoTablet is an OBJECT-typed media attribute (a WP media object: url/id/alt), not a CSS length — its own base sibling `photo` correctly carries css_property=NULL, so the row was self-inconsistent. ROOT CAUSE, proven not guessed: the derived layer (behavioural-analyser/css-property-classifications.json) claims css_property='max-width' + css_tier='tablet' because render.php:264 emits `sprintf('<source media="(max-width:1023px)" srcset="%s"', ...)` — the classifier read the media-query CONDITION inside an HTML <source> element's `media` ATTRIBUTE as if it were a CSS property emission. The breakpoints prove the mechanism beyond doubt: photoTablet took tier `tablet` from `max-width:1023px` and photoMobile took tier `mobile` from `max-width:767px` (render.php:261), which are exactly this project's tablet/mobile device-tier breakpoints. The tiers are rendered as <picture><source media> alternates (render.php:255-266), i.e. an art-direction source swap; nothing here emits a max-width DECLARATION, and style.css contains no max-width rule for the photo at all. Class checked comprehensively: the fingerprint (css_property='max-width' AND css_tier IS NOT NULL) returns exactly these two rows across the whole DB, and of the three files emitting `<source media=` only this block's inline sprintf trips it (sgs/responsive-logo and includes/helpers-media.php route through the shared helper). Overridden rather than fixed at the classifier because the classifier fix — teaching the behavioural analyser that a `media` attribute is not a CSS emission — is a shared-analyser change with real blast radius for a 2-row defect; the root cause is recorded here so that fix can be made deliberately later.

MIS-DERIVED css_property cleared 2026-08-29 — the mobile twin of the sgs/team-member.photoTablet entry directly above; see that entry for the full root cause. Here the derived layer claims css_property='max-width' + css_tier='mobile', read out of `<source media="(max-width:767px)">` at render.php:261. NOTE for anyone carrying forward the 2026-08-29 handoff prompt: that prompt stated `photoMobile` NO LONGER EXISTS in the DB, removed by the 2026-08-28 ghost-row prune. That is FALSE — re-verified against the live DB on 2026-08-29, both rows are present and both were mis-derived identically.

STRAY css_property cleared 2026-08-15. The attribute is NOT the emitter — the block's own docblock (render.php:14,21) states 'textAlign (native typography support — targets the headline child)' and 'textAlign is handled by the single native textAlign support'. block.json confirms supports.typography.textAlign=true, and the headline element's attrMap routes css:text-align to `native:typography.textAlign`, NOT to this attr. The bare `textAlign` string attribute is a vestigial declaration; its css_property='text-align' was a rogue seed the derived classifier never claims, so db-consistency flagged it as 'would vanish on the next reseed'. Pinning it to null makes the DB state match the truth durably instead of oscillating each reseed.

2026-08-28 routing-collision fix. `columns` does NOT paint grid-template-columns: render.php:477 emits the CUSTOM PROPERTY `--sgs-card-grid-columns` (plus -tablet/-mobile), which style.css:5-7 then feeds into `grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--sgs-card-grid-columns,3),1fr)`. The standard derivation assigned `grid-template-columns` from the property_suffixes row `Columns -> grid-template-columns`, which is correct for a track-list attr and wrong for a COUNT. That mis-derivation made `columns` contend with `gridTemplateColumns` (declared in the `grid` element's own attrMap) for the SAME routing slot: db-consistency Check #1 reported amb:sgs/card-grid:grid-template-columns:wrapper_css:wrapper:None:None, where the resolver silently picks by rowid. css_element cannot separate them here -- unlike sgs/post-grid (columns=inner, gridTemplateColumns=wrapper, two real nodes), card-grid puts `sgs-card-grid` AND the uid class on ONE element (render.php:456-462), so both genuinely resolve to the same node. Naming the custom property is the truthful disambiguation, and it is what this file's _doc calls a code-DOES vs code-MEANS record (cf. sgs/tabs tabIndicatorColour). Effect: gridTemplateColumns becomes the sole owner of grid-template-columns -- correct, because it is also the one that WINS in the browser (equal specificity, wrapper's inline <style id=uid> emitted after the lifted style.css) and the only one able to express asymmetric tracks a clone may carry.
